rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الصابئون is nominative rather than governed by إنّ, which would require the accusative; it can be an independent or parenthetical subject with an omitted predicate, and the Nasara coordinate to إنّ's noun.
rows.anchor: ولو أراد إنّ لنصب كلمة (الصابئون) . إذن لماذا لم ينصب (الصابئون)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the Sabians before the Christians does not rank them as superior; it suits the passage's criticism of Christian claims that God is one of three and that Christ is God.
rows.anchor: ليس بالضرورة أن يكون التقديم للأفضل ولكن التقديم هنا لمقتضى السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative marks the Sabians as the least-ranked and furthest astray among those named, while the Christians' more serious condition is expressed by their coordination as People of the Book.
rows.anchor: لكن رفعها للدلالة على أنهم (الصابئون) أبعد المذكورين في الضلال ولأنهم أقلّ منزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabaʾ is more momentous than khabar, and the verb anbaʾ is stronger than akhbara; broadcasters should say نشرة الأنباء for major news and نشرة الأخبار for ordinary news.
rows.anchor: والصيغة الفعلية للنبأ (أنبأ) أقوى أيضاً منها للخبر (أخبر)

rows.speaker: النحاة
rows.claim: Grammarians call أن after لما زائد; removing it does not change the general meaning. The question contrasts its use in al-Qasas with passages about Lot in Hud and Yusuf.
rows.anchor: هذه عند النُحاة زائدة إذا وقعت (أن) بعد لما فهي زائدة أي لا تؤثر على المعنى العام إذا حُذفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hayawan is a verbal noun on the faʿalan pattern, like gathayan, fayadan, dawaran, and ghaliyan.
rows.anchor: الحيوان: مصدر على وزن فعلان مثل غثيان وفيضان ودوران وغليان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern conveys continuous movement and renewal: the afterlife is active, without sleep, while worldly life is like sleep beside it; hayat alone would suggest fluctuation, so hayawan fits.
rows.anchor: صيغة في المصادر تدلّ على الحركة المستمرة والحدوث وهي أعلى أنواع الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sole garden formula without من is in 9:100 and indicates rivers do not begin beneath the gardens, a lower rank; the foremost migrants and helpers are mentioned without prophets, unlike other garden passages.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (جنات تجري تحتها الأنهار) دلالة على أن بداية الجريان ليس من تحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anzafa/yunzifuna has two senses: to become drunk and lose one's reason, or, intransitively, for the drink to run out.
rows.anchor: أنزف يُنزف بمعنى سكِر وبمعنى نفذ شرابه وانقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Saffat describes other servants at a lower degree, while al-Waqiʿa describes the few forerunners at the highest ranks of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وردت في عباد الله الآخِرين وهم أقلّ درجة من السابقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Waqiʿa gives the forerunners fruit to choose and desired bird meat, exceeding al-Saffat's known fruits and honor without choice.
rows.anchor: ذكر (وفاكهة مما يتخيرون ولحم طير مما يشتهون) في الآية تخيير وزيادة لحم طير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being brought near in al-Waqiʿa is an added degree beyond being honored in al-Saffat.
rows.anchor: التقريب هو الإكرام وزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Waqiʿa adds inlaid couches and reclining to the facing seats mentioned in al-Saffat, describing greater luxury.
rows.anchor: التنعّم هنا أكثر: موضونة، إتّكاء، تقابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Waqiʿa identifies the immortal youths serving them, whereas al-Saffat uses a passive construction without naming the servers.
rows.anchor: (يطوف عليهم ولدان مخلدون) تحديد الولدان المخلدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Waqiʿa adds cups and jugs beside the cup of flowing drink, giving a wider variety of vessels for varied drinks.
rows.anchor: زيادة وتنويع في الأواني لتنوع الأشربة

words: لا فيها غول ولا هم يُنزفون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghawl may mean spoilage or destruction, or impairment of the mind; if the latter, it overlaps with yunzifun, but ghawl describes the drink and yunzifun its drinker.
rows.anchor: الغول إما للإفساد والإهلاك وإما اغتيال العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Saffat's denial of ghawl does not itself deny headache; al-Waqiʿa denies headache, drunkenness, and depleted drink, which the author treats as greater honor for the forerunners.
rows.anchor: (لا يصدّعون عنها ولا يُنزفون) لا يصيبهم صداع ونفي الصداع نفي لما هو أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When worship expands and becomes more general, the author says the masculine verb and lam in the oath response suit it; the narrower first case used qad and a feminine verb.
rows.anchor: فعندما اتسعت العبادة وصارت أعمّ وأوسع من الأولى ذكّر وجاء باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A broken plural permits either masculine or feminine agreement, as shown by masculine angels in Sad and feminine agreement in Aal Imran.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يؤنّث الفعل أو يُذكّر إذا كان الجمع جمع تكسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angel worship verbs take masculine agreement; the author says masculine worship is more complete and notes that all messengers were men.
rows.anchor: لأن المذكر في العبادة أكمل من عبادة الأنثى ولذلك جاء الرسل كلهم رجالاً.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commands addressed to angels consistently use masculine forms, including اسجدوا, أنبئوني, and فقعوا له ساجدين.
rows.anchor: (اسجدوا، أنبئوني، فقعوا له ساجدين)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verbs following mention of the angels are masculine, as in their entering, witnessing, and glorifying God.
rows.anchor: كل فعل يقع بعد ذكر الملائكة يأتي بالتذكير أيضاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nominal descriptions of angels use masculine forms, including al-muqarrabun, basitu aydihim, musawwimin, murdifin, and munzilin.
rows.anchor: كل وصف إسمي للملائكة يأتي بالتذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acts of angel worship use masculine forms; the author says masculine worship is more complete and that the messengers were all men.
rows.anchor: لأن المذكر في العبادة أكمل من عبادة الأنثى ولذلك جاء الرسل كلهم رجالاً.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Strength and severity favor masculine forms, especially for the harsher of two punishments; the author contrasts masculine yatwaffa with feminine tawaffat and also compares forms of tanzil.
rows.anchor: كل أمر فيه شِدّة وقوة حتى لو كان عذابين أحدهما أشدّ من الآخر فالأشدّ يأتي بالتذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic glad tidings from angels never use masculine agreement; they always come in feminine forms such as fanadathu and qalati al-malaika.
rows.anchor: لم تأت بشرى بصيغة التذكير أبداً في القرآن الكريم فكل بشارة في القرآن الكريم تأتي بصيغة التأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tur adds the accusation of soothsaying because it also reports accusations of madness, poetry, and fabrication; al-Qalam names madness alone.
rows.anchor: ذكروا أنه كاهن، وذكروا أنه مجنون، وذكروا أنه شاعر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tur's verse about a ladder and a listener fits the soothsayer accusation because soothsayers claim to listen to their jinn followers.
rows.anchor: والاستماع مما تدعيه الكهنة لتابعيهم من الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tur also mentions magic, which makes the added reference to soothsayers fitting.
rows.anchor: ذكر السحر في سورة الطور فقال: (أفسحر هذا أم أنتم لا تبصرون) . فناسب ذكر السحر ذكرَ الكهنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expanded list of soothsayer, madman, poet, and liar accusations also suits al-Tur's many opening oaths, compared with al-Qalam's single oath.
rows.anchor: توسع في القسم في أول سورة الطور بخلاف سورة القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qalam's opening denial of madness answers the closing charge that the Prophet is mad, making the end correspond to the beginning.
rows.anchor: فرد عليهم في أول السورة بنفي الجنون عنه فقال: (ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون) . فناسب آخر السورة أولها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic ba reinforces negation in bi-majnun, while the emphatic lam reinforces the disbelievers' positive assertion la-majnun.
rows.anchor: الباء لتوكيد النفي واللام لتوكيد الإثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abadan suits detailed accounts of reward or punishment and may also mark the severity deserved by an act.
rows.anchor: هناك أمران: إذا كان هناك تفصيل في الجزاء يقول (أبداً) تكون مناسبة، تفصيل الجزاء سواء في العقاب أو الثواب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abadan does not itself mean endless permanence or no exit; khulud alone carries that sense, while khulud literally means remaining and can sometimes mean a long time.
rows.anchor: (أبداً) لا تحمل معنى التأبيد الدائم أو عدم الخروج لأن الخلود وحده يحمل هذا المعنى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafjir means bringing water out abundantly; inbijas is a lesser degree, and إخراج is less still.
rows.anchor: التفجير هو إخراج الماء بغزارة. والانبجاس أقل من التفجير والإخراج أقل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported explanation takes ghiyabat al-jubb as the well's bottom or end, hidden from a viewer's sight.
rows.anchor: يقولون إما قعر الجُبّ أي نهايته ثم غيبته عن عين الناظر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported explanation takes it as a cave within the well, called ghiyaba because it is hidden from the viewer.
rows.anchor: قسم يقولون هو كهف في الجب ويسمى غيابة لأنه غائب عن عين الناظر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jubb is a well with water, as the bucket drawn in Yusuf shows; Joseph was to be placed out of sight, while a biʾr may be dry or abandoned.
rows.anchor: الجُبّ يعني البئر الذي فيه الماء كما توضح الآية (وَجَاءتْ سَيَّارَةٌ فَأَرْسَلُواْ وَارِدَهُمْ فَأَدْلَى دَلْوَهُ (19) يوسف)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasṭir means writing; unlike kataba, which may be only a letter, two letters, or a word, satar implies a larger amount of writing.
rows.anchor: يسطر أي يكتب والفرق بين سطر وكتب أن الكتابة قد تكون حرفاً واحداً أو حرفين أو كلمة أما السطر فالكتابة أكثر

rows.speaker: النحاة
rows.claim: Grammarians treat the phrase as one oath: the pen is sworn by, and what they write is coordinated to the oath and inherits its force; N is a disconnected letter like Qaf.
rows.anchor: النحاة يرون أنه قسم واحد ونعطف عليه وليس قسماً مستقلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinated phrase what they write shares the oath's syntactic and semantic status, just as coordinated sentence parts share their grammatical role.
rows.anchor: المعطوف على الشيء له حكمه فالمعطوف على المبتدأ مبتدأ والمعطوف على الخبر خبر والمعطوف على الفاعل فاعل فالحكم واحد والإخبار عنهم واحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waw and fa can coordinate additional oath objects to the first oath even though fa itself is not an oath particle, as in the sequence of al-Naziat.
rows.anchor: ثم جاء بالفاء وهي ليست حرف قسم وإنما حرف عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra ba in al-Qalam's opening denial matches the closing accusation of madness, since the disbelievers add no charge beyond what the opening refutes.
rows.anchor: فزيادة الباء (بمجنون) لأنه لم يزد الكافرون عما جاء في الآيات فناسب أول السورة ما جاء في آخرها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ba emphasizes a negation, whereas lam emphasizes an affirmation; inn with lam intensifies the disbelievers' assertion about the Prophet.
rows.anchor: والباء تأتي لتوكيد النفي (بمجنون) واللام لتوكيد الإيجاب (لمجنون) فهو نفي مقابل للام التوكيد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Munafiqun places wealth before children in warning believers not to let either distract them from God's remembrance, since those who do so are losers.
rows.anchor: قدّم الأموال على الأولاد وعزاه إلى عدم الإنشغال بالأموال والأولاد عن ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilhaʾ is preferred to shughul because it generally occurs in blame, and neglecting remembrance of God is more apt to this rebuke than mere busyness.
rows.anchor: الإلهاء على العموم يستخدم في مقام الذم ثم إن الإلتهاء عن ذكر الله أولى من ذكر الشغل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qalam's hammaz suits its focus on social conduct: it lists bad traits and commands nonobedience, with little outcome detail beyond branding; al-Humaza describes the end in detail.
rows.anchor: أما في سورة القلم استخدام صيغة (همّاز) لأن الكلام في التعامل مع الناس وكل سورة القلم تتكلم عن التعامل مع الناس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and sons can induce submission despite their owner's wrongdoing; the verse says not to obey such a person, and the author extends the point to powerful nations dominating weaker peoples.
rows.anchor: ولو كان ذا مال وبنين فهو يمتنع بماله وبنيه والمال والبنون هما سبب الخضوع والإيضاح والإنقياد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic repetition is part of its inimitability; the first clause is joined by fa, and the second verse joins with thumma.
rows.anchor: الآية فيها عطف على جزء من الآية بالفاء ثم عطف بـ (ثمّ) في الآية الثانية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The list escalates by rank: faultfinding needs no movement, carrying tales harms more, withholding good harms further, aggression is worse, and athim gathers kinds of evil.
rows.anchor: والهماز هو العيّاب وذلك لا يفتقر إلى حركة وانتقال من موضعه بخلاف النميم.

rows.speaker: بدائع الفوائد
rows.claim: Bada'i al-Fawa'id explains the ranking: a faultfinder need not move unlike a tale-bearer, and withholding good from oneself precedes aggression against others.
rows.anchor: جاء في بدائع الفوائد: وأما تقدم همّاز على مشّاء بنميم فالرتبة لأن المشي مرتب على القعود في المكان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In threatening contexts, hearing comes before knowledge because hearing sounds and whispers makes God seem nearer and more threatening, although His knowledge covers the hidden and the manifest.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه خبر يتضمن التخويف والتهديد. فبدأ بالسمع لتعلقه كالأصوات وهمس الحركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also offers a simpler ordering rationale: hearing is one of the means of knowledge, so it precedes knowledge.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال: إن السمع من وسائل العلم فهو يسبقه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāʾat is used for the harsher arrival of the Resurrection, while atat is used for the lighter worldly crisis from which God may rescue people if He wills.
rows.anchor: فالموقف الأول أشق وأشد مما في الثانية، فجاء بالفعل (جاء) دون (أتى) بخلاف الآية الثانية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first passage depicts deniers at the afterlife, remorseful and bearing their burdens; the second is worldly, as people call on God and He may remove their affliction, unlike in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فإن الأولى في الآخرة وفي الذين كذبوا باليوم الآخر، وهم نادمون متحسرون على ما فرطوا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general pattern is jāʾa for what is difficult and severe, and ata for what is easier and lighter.
rows.anchor: فاتضح أن القرآن إنما يستعمل (جاء) لما هو أصعب وأشق. ويستعمل (أتى) لما هو أخف وأيسر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāʾa is heavier in sound and, the author says, appears in the Qur'an only in the past form, unlike ata in multiple conjugations; the heavier word suits the harder scene.
rows.anchor: ولعل من أسباب ذلك أن الفعل (جاء) أثقل من (أتى) في اللفظ
